title: Accurate Wichmann-Kroll vacuum polarization calculations with Gaussian basis set
authors: V. K. Ivanov, D. A. Glazov, A. V. Volotka
abstract: We apply a large Gaussian basis set of size up to $N = 500$ to calculate the all-order Wichmann-Kroll vacuum polarization correction in highly-charged ion. For a hydrogen-like system, this allows us to obtain an accurate correction value with a level of precision comparable to that of traditional methods. We demonstrate that values of effects that can be calculated as the difference between two quantities, such as the nuclear model correction, converge faster than the absolute value of the correction. We discuss the basis extrapolation methods and show their use in estimating the error due to incomplete convergence. Finally, we show an application of the Gaussian basis set to calculation of the vacuum polarization screening correction in lithium-like ions.
summary: This paper develops a highly accurate computational method using large Gaussian basis sets to calculate the Wichmann-Kroll vacuum polarization correction in heavy, highly-charged ions. It demonstrates the convergence properties of this calculation and successfully applies the technique to estimate the vacuum polarization screening effect in lithium-like atoms. The work is a significant theoretical advance in high-precision atomic structure calculations.
main_problem: The paper focuses on calculating the all-order Wichmann-Kroll vacuum polarization correction in highly-charged ions and investigating the vacuum polarization screening effect in lithium-like ions.
main_result: The use of a large Gaussian basis set (up to N=500) provides accurate results for the vacuum polarization correction, demonstrating that the difference between model corrections converges faster than the absolute value of the correction.
method: The calculations employ a finite-basis-set method using a Gaussian basis set to solve the Dirac equation, requiring advanced basis extrapolation techniques to estimate convergence errors.
model_or_system: The system involves hydrogen-like and lithium-like ions, governed by the Dirac equation. The calculations incorporate various nuclear charge distributions, including shell, sphere, and two-parameter Fermi models.
key_observables: The Wichmann-Kroll vacuum polarization energy correction (EWK) and the vacuum polarization screening energy shift ($\Delta E_{	ext{scr}}$).
important_parameters: Basis set size up to N=500, fine-structure constant alpha, and the atomic number Z (e.g., Z=92 for Uranium).
main_assumptions: The primary assumptions involve the applicability of the Gaussian basis set and the necessity of basis extrapolation methods to estimate the error due to incomplete convergence.
figures_summary: Figures show the radial vacuum polarization density partial components versus a convergence parameter $\beta$, illustrating monotonic convergence; other figures compare EWK components using different extrapolation methods.
paper_structure: The paper systematically calculates the WK correction using increasing basis sizes, compares results across different nuclear models, and then applies the methodology to calculate the screening effect in lithium-like ions using extrapolation techniques.
why_interesting: This work provides highly precise, advanced theoretical calculations for QED corrections in few-electron, highly-charged systems, which is fundamental for understanding atomic structure and is relevant to precision measurements in AMO physics.
